Please reload this page. * Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings * Fork 169 * Star * Code * Issues 165 * Pull requests 9 * Actions * Projects * Security and quality 52 * Insights Additional navigation options # Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in SSO/SAML Endpoint via Unencoded Exception Messages Moderate Fasse published GHSA-7jxv-38f3-6xgf Jul 20, 2026 ## Package admidio/admidio (Packagist (PHP)) ## Affected versions <= 5.0.10 ## Patched versions >= 5.0.11 ## Description ### Summary A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in Admidio's SSO/SAML endpoint (`modules/sso/index.php`). The outermost exception handler echoes exception messages directly to the HTTP response using `echo $e->getMessage()` without HTML encoding. Because the SAML request-processing branch lacks its own try/catch wrapper (unlike the OIDC branch), multiple attacker-controlled data paths — including the SAML Issuer element and LightSaml library query parameters — flow through exception messages into the unencoded output sink. No Content-Type header is explicitly set in the error path (defaults to `text/html`), and no Content-Security-Policy, X-XSS-Protection, or X-Content-Type-Options headers exist anywhere in the application. This allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who visits a crafted SSO/SAML URL, potentially leading to session hijacking, credential theft, and full account takeover — including administrator accounts. ### Details Root cause: `modules/sso/index.php` lines 108–109: } catch (Throwable $e) { echo $e->getMessage(); } The outermost `catch` block handles all uncaught exceptions from the SSO endpoint. It echoes the raw exception message to the HTTP response body without `htmlspecialchars()` or any HTML encoding. No `Content-Type` header is set in this error path, so PHP's default `text/html; charset=UTF-8` applies. Why the SAML branch reaches the outer catch without protection: The SAML branch at `index.php` lines 85–100 has no try/catch wrapper of its own, unlike the OIDC branch (lines 38–82): // SAML branch — NO try/catch: } elseif ($type === 'saml') { $samlService = new SAMLService($gDb, $gCurrentUser); // ... $samlService->handleSSORequest(); // line 92 — exceptions propagate to outer catch Inside `SAMLService::handleSSORequest()` (`src/SSO/Service/SAMLService.php:399`), the inner `try` block starts at line 415. However, lines 403–413 execute before that inner try and throw exceptions that propagate directly to the outer catch at `index.php:108`: // Line 403: static check — not exploitable if ($gSettingsManager->get('sso_saml_enabled') !== '1') { throw new Exception("SSO SAML is not enabled"); } // Line 407: BEFORE inner try — exploitable via LightSaml exceptions $request = $this->receiveMessage(); // Line 408: static check — not exploitable if (!$request instanceof AuthnRequest) { throw new Exception("Invalid request..."); } // Line 412–413: BEFORE inner try — exploitable via Issuer reflection $entityIdClient = $request->getIssuer()->getValue(); $client = $this->getClientFromID($entityIdClient); // Line 415: Inner try starts here — exceptions caught at line 600 try { Attack Vector 1 — SAML Issuer (EntityID) reflection (primary): 1. An attacker crafts a SAML AuthnRequest XML with a CDATA-wrapped XSS payload in the `` element. 2. The XML is Deflate-compressed, Base64-encoded, and sent as the `SAMLRequest` query parameter via HTTP-Redirect binding. 3. `receiveMessage()` (`SAMLService.php:407`) calls into LightSaml's `HttpRedirectBinding`, which reads `$_SERVER['QUERY_STRING']` directly (`HttpRedirectBinding.php` line 227), completely bypassing Admidio's `$_GET` sanitization (`strip_tags` in `global_request_params.php:29`). 4. The SAML XML is decoded, decompressed, and parsed by `DOMDocument::loadXML()`. 5. The Issuer element is deserialized by LightSaml's `AbstractNameID::deserialize()`, which calls `$this->setValue($node->textContent)`. Because the payload is in a CDATA section, `textContent` preserves the raw HTML characters (`<`, `>`, etc.). 6. `$request->getIssuer()->getValue()` at `SAMLService.php:412` returns the attacker's XSS payload string verbatim. 7. `$this->getClientFromID($entityIdClient)` at line 413 is called before the inner try block (line 415). 8. When no SAML client matches the XSS-string entityID, `SSOService.php:45` throws: throw new Exception("SSO client '$clientID' not found in database..."); 9. This exception propagates to the outer catch at `index.php:108`, where `echo $e->getMessage()` outputs the attacker's HTML/JavaScript directly into the response. Attack Vector 2 — LightSaml library exceptions with attacker-controlled data: The `receiveMessage()` call at line 407 is also outside the inner try. Multiple LightSaml exceptions include attacker-controlled strings: Exception | Source | LightSaml file | Pattern --- | --- | --- | --- `LightSamlBindingException` | `SAMLEncoding` query param | `HttpRedirectBinding.php:103` | `"Unknown encoding '%s'"` `LightSamlXmlException` | XML root element name | `SamlMessage.php:96` | `"Unknown SAML message '%s'"` `LightSamlXmlException` | XML namespace URI | `SamlMessage.php:73` | `"Invalid namespace '%s'..."` `LightSamlSecurityException` | `SigAlg` query param | `AbstractSignatureReader.php:91` | `"Unsupported signing algorithm: '%s'"` All propagate to `echo $e->getMessage()` at `index.php:109`. Why global input sanitization is bypassed: * `global_request_params.php:29` applies `strip_tags()` to `$_GET`. The `SAMLRequest` parameter is Base64-encoded (charset `[A-Za-z0-9+/=]`), which contains no `<` characters — `strip_tags` is a no-op. * LightSaml's `HttpRedirectBinding::parseQuery()` reads `$_SERVER['QUERY_STRING']` directly, bypassing `$_GET` entirely. * XML CDATA content passes through `DOMNode::$textContent` as raw text, preserving `<`, `>`, etc. * Entity-encoded XML (`<`, `>`) is decoded by `DOMDocument::loadXML()`, also producing raw characters. Missing mitigations (verified by grep across `src/` and `system/`): * No `htmlspecialchars()` or `SecurityUtils::encodeHTML()` at the output sink * No Content-Type header set in the error path * No Content-Security-Policy header anywhere in the application * No X-XSS-Protection header * No X-Content-Type-Options header ### PoC Prerequisites: SAML SSO must be enabled in Admidio settings (`sso_saml_enabled = 1`). Vector 1 — Issuer EntityID via CDATA (verified with Python simulation): Step 1: Craft a SAML AuthnRequest with CDATA-wrapped XSS payload: ]]> Step 2: Encode for SAML HTTP-Redirect binding (Deflate + Base64 + URL-encode): import base64, zlib, urllib.parse xml = ']]>' compressed = zlib.compress(xml.encode())[2:-4] b64 = base64.b64encode(compressed).decode() print(f"SAMLRequest={urllib.parse.quote(b64, safe='')}") Step 3: Send the crafted request (verified output): `GET /modules/sso/index.php/saml/sso?SAMLRequest=fZBBS0MxEIT%2FSsxJD7ax4GVJAo%2F2UtCLFg%2BWIiGuGvqSrbuJPP%2B98Z0UQZjTfjM7MFZCHk8wtPpW7vC9oVQ15bEIzMDpxgUoSBIoIaNAjXA%2F3N7AamHgxFQp0qh%2FRP5PBBHkmqhotd04%2FTSJfCCnl0%2BtHpClA6e7r1ORhtsiNZTaT2Z1fWmuunbGwKxH7e13H8xO9vZsv94Mu2FvU35VwtFNigoyE7sw9tLzZ4otY6mLSHRMeOEPB2%2BXv34s%2F67hvwA%3D%3D HTTP/1.1 Host: target-admidio.example.com ` Step 4: Server response (Content-Type defaults to text/html): `HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 SSO client '' not found in database. Please check the SSO client settings and configure the client in Admidio. ` The browser renders the `` tag, the `src=x` fails to load, and the `onerror` JavaScript handler executes, displaying the user's session cookie. Vector 2 — SAMLEncoding query parameter (simpler, no encoding required): `GET /modules/sso/index.php/saml/sso?SAMLRequest=anything&SAMLEncoding= HTTP/1.1 Host: target-admidio.example.com ` This triggers `LightSamlBindingException("Unknown encoding ''")` at `HttpRedirectBinding.php:103`, which propagates to `index.php:109` and is echoed raw. Negative/control case (confirmed): When SAML is not enabled, `handleSSORequest()` line 403 throws `Exception("SSO SAML is not enabled")` — a static message with no user-controlled data. No XSS occurs. Cleanup: No cleanup required — the PoC is stateless and does not modify any data. ### Impact This is a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability (CWE-79). It allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browsers of users who visit a crafted SSO/SAML URL. Impact includes: 1. Session hijacking: The attacker can steal session cookies or extract session tokens from the DOM, gaining full access to the victim's Admidio account. 2. Credential theft: If an administrator is targeted, the attacker can exfiltrate all member PII (names, emails, addresses, phone numbers). 3. Privilege escalation: By targeting an admin, the attacker can create new admin accounts, modify roles/permissions, or change system settings. 4. SSO trust chain compromise: Since this is the SSO IdP endpoint, compromising an admin session could allow manipulation of SAML/OIDC client configurations, potentially compromising all connected Service Providers. Who is impacted: Any Admidio instance where the SSO SAML feature is enabled (`sso_saml_enabled = 1`). The attack requires no authentication, no user interaction beyond visiting a URL, and can target any user including administrators. The SSO SAML feature was introduced in v5.0.0 and is a documented capability for Single Sign-On integration. ### Suggested remediation 1. HTML-encode all exception output at `modules/sso/index.php:109`: } catch (Throwable $e) { http_response_code(500); header('Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8'); echo htmlspecialchars($e->getMessage(), ENT_QUOTES | ENT_HTML5, 'UTF-8'); } 2. Wrap the SAML branch in its own try/catch at `modules/sso/index.php:85–100`, following the pattern already used by the OIDC branch: } elseif ($type === 'saml') { try { $samlService = new SAMLService($gDb, $gCurrentUser); // ... SAML endpoint routing ... } catch (Throwable $e) { http_response_code(500); header('Content-Type: application/json'); echo json_encode(['error' => 'SAML Error']); exit; } } 3. Add Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options headers globally. ### Credits * Thai Son Dinh from VinSOC Labs (R&D) ### CVE ID CVE-2026-69092 ### Severity Moderate 6.5 # CVSS overall score This score calculates overall vulnerability severity from 0 to 10 and is based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). #### CVSS v3 base metrics Attack vector Network Attack complexity Low Privileges required None User interaction None Scope Unchanged Confidentiality Low Integrity Low Availability None Learn more about base metrics # CVSS v3 base metrics Attack vector: More severe the more the remote (logically and physically) an attacker can be in order to exploit the vulnerability. If there are any questions or comments about this advisory, please email them to security@zitadel.com CVE-2026-29191 ## ZITADEL has 1-Click Account Takeover via XSS in /saml-post Endpoint Critical severity GitHub Reviewed Published Mar 4, 2026 in zitadel/zitadel • Updated Mar 9, 2026 ## Package github.com/zitadel/zitadel (Go) ## Affected versions >= 4.0.0, < 4.12.0 ## Patched versions 4.12.0 github.com/zitadel/zitadel/v2 (Go) >= 4.0.0, < 4.12.0 4.12.0 ## Description ### Summary A vulnerability was discovered in Zitadel's login V2 interface that allowed a possible account takeover. ### Impact Zitadel exposes an HTTP endpoint named /saml-post. This endpoint is used for handling requests to SAML IdPs and accepts two HTTP GET parameters: url and id. When these parameters are supplied, users’ browsers auto-submit an HTTP POST request to the provided url parameter. The endpoint insecurely redirects users using the provided url GET parameter. As a result, by specifying a javascript: scheme, malicious JS code could be executed on Zitadel users’ browsers. The endpoint also reflects user-supplied input in the server response, without HTML-encoding it. As a result, it is possible to inject arbitrary HTML code, which again leads to malicious JS code execution in the Zitadel users’ browsers. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit these XSS vulnerabilities, and thus, execute malicious JavaScript code on behalf of Zitadel users. By doing so, such an attacker could reset the password of their victims, and take over their accounts. It's important to note that this specific attack vector is mitigated for accounts that have Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) or Passwordless authentication enabled. ### Affected Versions Systems running one of the following versions are affected: * 4.x: `4.0.0` through `4.11.1` (including RC versions) Important Note: Although this /saml-post endpoint is used when Zitadel is integrated with a SAML Identity Provider (IdP), the vulnerability in this finding does not require Zitadel to be configured with a SAML IdP. Consequently, Zitadel is vulnerable in its default, out-of-the-box configuration. ### Patches The vulnerability has been addressed in the latest releases. The patch reworked the integration of SAML IdPs and the /saml-post endpoint no longer exists. Additionally, the page to change the password, now always requires the user's current password regardless of the state of the authenticated session. 4.x: Upgrade to >= 4.12.0 ### Workarounds The recommended solution is to upgrade to a patched version. If an upgrade is not possible and no SAML IdP integration is needed, a WAF or reverse proxy rule can be deployed to prevent access to the endpoint. ### Questions If there are any questions or comments about this advisory, please email them to security@zitadel.com ### Credits ZITADEL extends thanks once again to Amit Laish from GE Vernova for finding and reporting the vulnerability. ### References * GHSA-pr34-2v5x-6qjq * https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-29191 livio-a published to zitadel/zitadel Mar 4, 2026 Published to the GitHub Advisory Database Mar 4, 2026 Reviewed Mar 4, 2026 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- XSS via assertion consumer service URL in SAML POST-binding flow · Advisory · keycloak/keycloak · GitHub (https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/security/advisories/GHSA-8rmm-gm28-pj8q) 【turn113054search3】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2.5 years ago; Crawled: last month; # XSS via assertion consumer service URL in SAML POST-binding flow # XSS via assertion consumer service URL in SAML POST-binding flow High abstractj published GHSA-8rmm-gm28-pj8q Apr 17, 2024 ## Package org.keycloak.validation (Maven) ## Affected versions < 22.0.10, < 24.0.3 ## Patched versions 22.0.10, 24.0.3 ## Description Keycloak allows arbitrary URLs as SAML Assertion Consumer Service POST Binding URL (ACS), including JavaScript URIs (javascript:). If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please email us at security@zitadel.com # Stored XSS via Default URI Redirect in Login V2 High livio-a published GHSA-5wcj-9wj4-j65h Jun 22, 2026 ## Package ZITADEL (ZITADEL) ## Affected versions 4.0.0 - 4.15.2 ## Patched versions 4.15.3 ## Description ### Summary An incomplete fix for a previously resolved vulnerability allows organization or instance administrators to bypass safety checks for redirect URLs. While the remediation for GHSA-6rx5-m2rc-hmf7 successfully secured standard login redirect paths starting in version `4.12.0`, certain error screens in the OIDC and SAML login flows still mistakenly trust and use unvalidated, unsafe links without verifying their safety. ### Impact ZITADEL allows administrators to set a default redirect URL for an organization, determining where users are sent after certain authentication actions.
